question: Using Section 6D.02 and Figure 6D-1, which hand-signaling device is preferred, and how should it be displayed to stop traffic?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The STOP/SLOW paddle is the primary and preferred hand-signaling device for flaggers because it gives road users more positive guidance than red flags (flags are reserved for emergency situations). To stop traffic, the flagger must face road users and aim the STOP paddle face toward them in a stationary position with the arm extended horizontally, while holding the free arm with the palm above shoulder level toward approaching traffic. Standards (mandatory): - "To stop road users, the flagger shall face road users and aim the STOP paddle face toward road users in a stationary position with the arm extended horizontally away from the body. The free arm shall be held with the palm of the hand above shoulder level toward approaching traffic." Guidance (recommended): - "The STOP/SLOW paddle (see Figure 6D-1 and Table 6G-1) should be the primary and preferred hand-signaling device because the STOP/SLOW paddle gives road users more positive guidance than red flags." - Per Table 6G-1 (referenced in the Guidance evidence), the STOP face on the STOP/SLOW paddle (R1-1) is sized 18 x 18 inches. Support (informational): - The optimum display method is to place the STOP/SLOW paddle on a rigid staff tall enough that, when the end of the staff rests on the ground, the message is high enough to be seen by approaching or stopped traffic. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 6D-1 labels the STOP/SLOW paddle as the "PREFERRED METHOD" (with the flag for "EMERGENCY SITUATIONS ONLY") and depicts the "TO STOP TRAFFIC" posture — the flagger holding the 18-inch-minimum R1-1 STOP paddle on a staff with the free hand raised, palm toward traffic. [Image 2] shows the same Figure 6D-1 in its full-page context, confirming the paddle column as the preferred method and the flag column as limited to emergencies. [Image 3] shows the text of Section 6D.05, including the mandatory paddle-signaling method for stopping road users. Citations: - Section 6D.02 Guidance §1 (p.783) - Section 6D.05 Standard §3 (p.785) - Section 6D.02 Support §5 (p.783) - Figure 6D-1 (p.784)
gold_answer: The STOP/SLOW paddle is the primary and preferred device. To stop traffic, the flagger faces traffic, displays the STOP face in a stationary position, and raises the free arm with the palm toward traffic.
